text: Found it: in /gin/errors.go, `Unwrap()` is declared on the pointer receiver `*Error`, while `Error()` (the method that makes `Error` satisfy the `error` interface) is on the value receiver. So a plain `Error` value satisfies `error` but does NOT expose `Unwrap`, and the `errors.Is`/`errors.As` chain stops dead at it. Fixing it by moving `Unwrap` to the value receiver — ETA a few minutes.

Fixed and verified. In /gin/errors.go, `Unwrap()` now uses a value receiver:

    func (msg Error) Unwrap() error { return msg.Err }

so a plain `Error` value (which already satisfied `error` via the value-receiver `Error() string`) now also participates in the `errors.Is`/`errors.As`/`errors.Unwrap` chain. Both `errors.Is(wrapped, innerErr)` and `errors.As(wrapped, &target)` now return true for the value form, and the pointer form still works.

Checks run: full `go test ./...` passes (same as baseline, no regressions), `TestErrorUnwrap` passes, and a temporary test exercising the value form passed (and failed before the change, confirming it exercised the bug). The temp file was removed; `git status` shows only errors.go modified.

Confirmed: `responseWriter.WriteHeader` in /gin/response_writer.go logs the "Headers were already written" warning but then still overwrites `w.status`, so `Status()` reports a code that was never sent. Fix: return early in the already-written branch so the recorded status stays 200. Applying and verifying now (ETA ~5 min).

Fixed and verified. In /gin/response_writer.go, `WriteHeader` now returns early in the already-written branch:

    if w.Written() {
        debugPrint("[WARNING] Headers were already written. Wanted to override status code %d with %d", w.status, code)
        return
    }

So after `WriteHeader(200)` + `WriteHeaderNow()`, a later `WriteHeader(401)` only logs the warning and leaves `Status()` at 200, matching what the client actually received. Before the response is written, `WriteHeader` still sets the status normally.

Checks: full `go test ./...` passes with no regressions vs baseline; a temporary test reproducing your scenario failed before the change (`Status() = 401, want 200`) and passes after; the temp file was removed, and only errors.go (previous request) and response_writer.go are modified.
